channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-13
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 117 news received.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation ends a turbulent period for Nvidia, after he transformed gaming chips into the engine of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Huang’s Departure Alarms Investors Across the AI Sector
item.description: The Nvidia leader’s resignation is weakening the company’s stock and raising fears of repercussions for companies across the artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: Huang’s Departure Could Change the Outlook for Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: Nvidia’s planned $10 billion investment could be reassessed, while future chip deals could slow. The departure could also strengthen Anthropic’s position in Washington and its chip-diversification strategy.

item.title: OpenAI Security Officials Tricked by Fake Russian Agents
item.description: Three senior OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes on a video call with Russian scammers posing as Ukraine’s intelligence chief. OpenAI has opened an investigation and taken steps to prevent a recurrence.

item.title: Groups Call for a Freeze on New AI Models
item.description: Four nonprofit organizations asked a San Francisco judge to halt new frontier models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI.

item.title: OpenAI Reportedly Supports Bills Restricting China’s Access to AI Chips
item.description: OpenAI reportedly told lawmakers it would support bipartisan bills restricting China’s access to artificial intelligence chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Reportedly Six Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO reportedly attracted about six times more demand than the number of shares offered. During its roadshow, the company also said Claude had been ported to AMD GPUs in three days, compared with several months previously.

item.title: SpaceX Announces $74 Billion in AI Computing Sites
item.description: SpaceX announced $74 billion in investments in AI-dedicated computing sites, including a $50 billion site in Arizona and a $24 billion gas-powered complex near Starbase.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Personal Agents Now Support Custom Instructions
item.description: ChatGPT’s personal agents can now follow custom instructions, such as writing only in lowercase or displaying a draft before sending an email.

item.title: Could the Touchscreen MacBook Pro Replace the M5 iPad Pro?
item.description: The touchscreen MacBook Pro supports macOS apps and offers substantial memory and storage, but it does not work with the Apple Pencil. It starts at $2,899, compared with $999 for the M5 iPad Pro.

item.title: Starlink limits the speed of Ukrainian drones
item.description: Starshield, Starlink’s military version, is reportedly cutting the satellite connection to Ukrainian equipment traveling faster than 161 km/h again. This limit prevents interceptor drones from pursuing certain Russian drones flying at up to 400 km/h.

item.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights
item.description: United Airlines will block unauthorized third-party AI agents that attempt to book, purchase, or manage trips through its channels. The airline cites privacy, account security, and federal aviation regulations, among other reasons.

item.title: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a specialized AI model
item.description: Google has launched Gemini Decision 1, a low-cost model designed to answer binary, multiple-choice, or rating questions. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and also provides a confidence score.

item.title: AlphaGenome 2 links genetic mutations to cell types
item.description: Google DeepMind has launched AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts the effect of genetic variants on specific types of human cells. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identified about 30% of causal variants, compared with 16% previously.

item.title: Companies offer high salaries and luxury travel to attract AI talent
item.description: Companies are offering generous compensation and luxury travel to compete for artificial intelligence talent.

item.title: ChatGPT Lets Businesses Claim Their Profiles for Free
item.description: OpenAI is launching Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta space where eligible businesses can claim a verified profile, track their mentions, and create a conversational agent. Profiles are free, but agents are initially available to online retailers and digital services in the United States.

item.title: Claude Launches Sheets, Whiteboards, and Narrated Data Videos
item.description: Anthropic is launching Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, new workspace tools. Claude Data can connect to Snowflake and Salesforce to create dashboards, visual stories, or short narrated videos, while Sheets lets users build spreadsheets and Whiteboards enables collaboration on a shared board.

item.title: Nvidia Reportedly Preparing to Fire Jensen Huang After Another Affair
item.description: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire CEO Jensen Huang after the Wall Street Journal reported a second affair, this time with another company executive.

item.title: Blue Unveils a Smartphone That Manages Apps for the User
item.description: Blue is developing a phone that acts as a chief of staff for apps, handling repetitive tasks and showing only important information. The Y Combinator-backed startup is testing its beta version with former iPhone users.

item.title: ChatGPT Launches a Personal Finance Tool in Its Desktop App
item.description: ChatGPT’s personal finance tool is available in the desktop app for all plans. It provides personalized answers about users’ money and spending.

item.title: Adobe will open Photoshop and its other Creative Cloud apps to AI assistants
item.description: Adobe plans to let assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude directly modify content in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects through Model Context Protocol integrations. The feature is expected to enter private beta in early 2027 and aims to automate repetitive tasks while preserving manual control.

item.title: Anthropic Signs Up to $4.3 Billion in Cloud Deals with Microsoft
item.description: Anthropic has expanded its cloud computing agreements with Microsoft for up to $4.3 billion. The company is seeking more infrastructure capacity ahead of its planned IPO.

item.title: Anthropic Reportedly Surpasses OpenAI in Revenue with Far Lower Losses
item.description: Anthropic reportedly generated $17 billion in revenue in the third quarter, compared with $10 billion for OpenAI, while posting far lower operating losses. OpenAI is accelerating its enterprise sales and could cut prices to close the gap.

item.title: A Young Founder Named Jensen Huang Benefits from His Namesake’s Troubles
item.description: Jensen Huang, a 24-year-old Singaporean founder, explains why the negative press surrounding Nvidia’s CEO benefits his company.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Departure Does Not Solve Nvidia’s Problems
item.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation begins a period of instability for Nvidia. Its organizational structure and lack of a succession plan leave many problems to resolve.

item.title: Founder Jensen Huang Had Become Nvidia’s Biggest Risk
item.description: Jensen Huang built the Nvidia empire, but the company’s dependence on him has now become a major risk.

item.title: Nvidia’s Structure Complicates Its Transition After Huang’s Departure
item.description: Flat organizations built around powerful founders can be effective, but they become problematic when their leader is gone.

item.title: Small Investors Keep Buying Nvidia Shares
item.description: Despite Nvidia’s stock decline and Wall Street’s pessimism after Jensen Huang’s resignation, some retail investors are taking advantage of the drop to buy more shares.

item.title: Wall Street Analysts Turn Away from Nvidia
item.description: After revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationships and his departure, Wall Street analysts have become more negative on Nvidia’s stock.

item.title: Warby Parker Launches Smart Glasses to Compete with Meta’s
item.description: Warby Parker’s smart glasses use technologies from Google and Samsung. Business Insider tested them to determine how they differ from Meta’s glasses.

item.title: Silicon Valley Prepares for a Future Without Jensen Huang
item.description: At the Cerebral Valley AI Summit, founders and investors warned that Huang’s departure could hurt startups and destabilize an industry that views Nvidia as its “central bank.”

item.title: The United States Faces a Growing Population Shortage
item.description: Falling birth rates, immigration and tourism are creating a “Great People Shortage.” Areas dependent on newcomers are expected to feel the effects first.

item.title: TikTok Centralizes Its U.S. E-Commerce Operations in China
item.description: TikTok has placed its U.S. e-commerce operations under the responsibility of Chinese executives. Business Insider obtained the organizational chart for the 14 top executives and their teams.

item.title: Instacart Partners with Provi to Supply Bars
item.description: Instacart has partnered with Provi. The platform will offer same-day delivery to bars and restaurants for nonalcoholic items such as mixers and garnishes.

item.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Email for Many Companies
item.description: A Microsoft outage is disrupting email, even as some business executives use it very little.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Leather Jackets Have Become a Joke
item.description: Jensen Huang’s once-iconic leather jackets are now being mocked following the controversies surrounding the Nvidia leader.

item.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool to Address Labor Shortages
item.description: Anthropic is offering a new Claude tool designed to help manufacturers facing labor shortages.

item.title: Flowers Left Outside Nvidia Headquarters After Huang’s Resignation
item.description: Photos show flowers left outside Nvidia headquarters following Jensen Huang’s resignation.

item.title: Amazon’s Ring Flying Camera Raises Questions About Its Target Audience
item.description: The Amazon Ring Drone Cam product has prompted questions about who it is intended for.

item.title: Michael Burry Advises Selling Nvidia Stock
item.description: Investor Michael Burry recommends getting out of Nvidia stock.

item.title: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s Cousin, Leads Nvidia Rival AMD
item.description: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s cousin, is the CEO of AMD, an Nvidia competitor.

item.title: Alice Huang Barred from Returning to Singapore
item.description: Singapore says Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive involved in the Nvidia scandal, is not permitted to return to the country.

item.title: RLHF Is Costly Mainly Because of Its Training Loop
item.description: In RLHF, the infrastructure costs of maintaining four models simultaneously during PPO can exceed annotation expenses. DPO reuses the same preference data without a separate reward model, making it a simpler starting point for most teams.

item.title: Cerebras Reports $230.9 Million in Third-Quarter Revenue
item.description: Cerebras reported $230.9 million in third-quarter revenue, up 70%, and raised its full-year guidance.

item.title: FBI Dismantles North Korean Cryptocurrency Theft Campaign
item.description: The FBI disrupted North Korea’s FaceStealer campaign, which used fake Zoom-style meetings featuring recordings of people known to the victims to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency.

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a Cheaper Model for Coding and Agents
item.description: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a fast, lower-cost model for everyday coding and agent work. It is available in the Gemini app, the Gemini API and AI Studio.

item.title: Google Prepares Gemini Glasses with Translation in More Than 70 Languages
item.description: Google announced Gemini glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster offering hands-free navigation and translation in more than 70 languages. They will be sold starting at $395 in the United States and South Korea, with in-store availability beginning December 10.

item.title: Yogurt Summarizes Calls Without Sending a Bot to the Meeting
item.description: Yogurt records calls without having a bot join the meeting, then produces a free summary with next steps assigned to each person. The project is presented as free and open source.

item.title: Pomerado Turns API-Less Websites into Tools for Coding Agents
item.description: Pomerado turns a website without an API, such as a vendor invoice portal, into a tool that a coding agent can use from a single prompt. The service offers a free plan followed by a $50-per-month option.

item.title: Kiln Runs AI Models Directly in the Browser
item.description: Kiln runs conversational, transcription and image models directly in the browser from Hugging Face files, without a server or conversion step. The project is presented as free and open source.

item.title: Spotify DJ Adds Nine Voices and an Option to Turn Off Commentary
item.description: Spotify Premium DJ offers nine new voices and a setting to disable most commentary between songs while retaining personalized recommendations.

item.title: Disney Expands Adobe Partnership for Its Parks, Films and ESPN Content
item.description: Disney is using Adobe’s custom Firefly Foundry models to speed up art design, visual effects and ESPN content. The shorter iteration times also raise questions about work methods and staffing.

item.title: Google Gemini Shows What It Remembers About Users and Lets Them Correct It
item.description: Gemini displays and lets users edit the information it remembers about them in a summary organized into five timestamped categories. However, deleting a memory may not erase the source conversation.

item.title: Microsoft Teams rolls out AI detection of phishing attempts
item.description: Microsoft Teams is rolling out AI-powered detection of impersonation and social engineering in chats, even without a malicious link. Warnings about deepfakes in meetings will follow, but will require third-party configuration.

item.title: Southeast Asian anti-scam hub offers free training
item.description: The Scam Ready ASEAN hub offers free training, an interactive game and country-specific reporting contacts across 11 nations. Scams cost Southeast Asia $23.6 billion.

item.title: Meta AI: features, pricing and user guide
item.description: Meta AI is integrated into Meta’s apps, with features powered by Muse, multiple pricing tiers and privacy controls. The guide covers platform availability and use of Incognito mode, among other topics.

item.title: Part 5: Automating repetitive tasks with AI
item.description: The final part of the playbook explains how to document your system, connect beehiiv to AI, and automate recurring tasks. It also shows how to turn the most engaged readers into customers and build a prompt library.

item.title: Guide: Creating a B2B newsletter that generates leads
item.description: This guide explains how to write for an ideal customer, use your newsletter as a CRM, and measure leads rather than just opens.

item.title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production through summer 2027
item.description: Tesla will continue producing the Cybertruck through the end of summer 2027 to clear its order backlog, according to Elon Musk. The lineup has been reduced to the Cyberbeast alone, priced at around $110,000.

item.title: Roku abandons its smart home ambitions
item.description: Roku is abandoning its ambitions in the smart home sector.

item.title: AWS offers a free local equivalent of its cloud
item.description: AWS is offering developers a free local equivalent of its cloud services, built by AI agents.

item.title: IBM aims to link two quantum chips to reach 1,040 qubits
item.description: IBM plans to link two quantum chips to create a 1,040-qubit system in 2027.

item.title: Helsing launches Clarity, a European rival to Palantir’s Maven
item.description: Helsing is launching Clarity, a European solution presented as a rival to Palantir’s Maven.

item.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI exposes Notion conversations
item.description: A cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access transcripts of conversations involving Notion customers.

item.title: Gemini comes to Apple CarPlay
item.description: Gemini is now available on Apple CarPlay.

item.title: Reddit resisted U.S. and German demands to identify users
item.description: Reddit rejected attempts by U.S. and German authorities to unmask certain users.

item.title: Apple HomeView: A limited but promising launch
item.description: An analysis of Apple HomeView describes a limited launch with significant potential.

item.title: Howard Lutnick does not want to halt Nvidia chip exports
item.description: Howard Lutnick reportedly does not want to stop the flow of Nvidia chips overseas.

item.title: Complex AI agent architectures cost up to 4.7 times more
item.description: An analysis of agents designed for professional workflows finds no dominant design. Multi-step architectures cost up to 4.7 times more and introduce up to 5.8 times more latency, with gains that are rarely sufficient.

item.title: Studies on AI medical scribes use 96 different metrics
item.description: AI medical scribes are evaluated using 96 metrics across 54 studies, one-third of which are used by only a single study. The results are therefore difficult to compare and rarely account for safety or patient outcomes.

item.title: Processing underrepresented languages can cost up to ten times more
item.description: Models charge up to ten times more to process underrepresented languages such as Amharic. A Portuguese-designed vocabulary reduces costs for Guarani and Quechua by about 24%.

item.title: One-third of U.S. adults have left an online community
item.description: According to a Pew Research Center survey, about one-third of U.S. adults say they have left an online community. More than eight in ten cite declining interest.

item.title: Adobe Adds Video, Music, and Sound Generation to Premiere
item.description: Adobe is adding tools to Premiere for generating video, sound effects, ambience, and music directly in the timeline. These tools rely on models from Adobe Firefly, Google, Kling, Runway, and Luma.

item.title: Google Makes Gemini 4 Carbon Available After Limited Rollout
item.description: Google has made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week limited rollout to cybersecurity advocates. The model is accessible through Gemini, AI Mode in Search, and Antigravity.

item.title: Anthropic Publishes a Guide to Choosing the Right Claude Model
item.description: Anthropic published a guide explaining how to choose the appropriate Claude model for each task. It recommends, among other things, pairing cheaper models with simple tasks and more powerful models with ambitious projects.

item.title: Who Is Kimberly Powell, the Former Nvidia Executive Linked to Jensen Huang?
item.description: The article profiles Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive accused of having a relationship with CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: Elon Musk Says He Would Hire Jensen Huang
item.description: Elon Musk said he would hire Jensen Huang.

item.title: China Would Be the Main Beneficiary of Jensen Huang’s Downfall
item.description: The article analyzes why China would be the main beneficiary of Jensen Huang’s downfall.

item.title: Grok Bot becomes a proactive colleague for teams
item.description: With Grok Bot 1.0, the agent can handle tasks without being prompted, retain a shared memory of the organization, and communicate in Slack or Microsoft Teams. It is available now and learns from teams’ feedback and preferences.

item.title: Natura Is Preparing a Smart Ring with a Voice Agent
item.description: Natura is developing a steel ring with a button for requesting help, recording ideas, and launching voice agents on nearby devices. It will also track sleep, heart rate, and steps, with a Kickstarter launch and deliveries planned for December or January.

item.title: Three New AI-Powered Scams Exploit Voices, Images, and Personal Data
item.description: Fraudsters are using AI to analyze public posts, clone voices, and create fake images or videos to personalize their attacks. The scams discussed include contextual spear phishing, fake video calls from a CEO, and ransom demands involving supposedly missing pets.

item.title: Yandex Recovers 97% of Data Affected by Drone Attacks
item.description: Russian cloud provider Yandex recovered about 97% of customer data affected by drone strikes on three data centers in October. The remaining 2.84% is permanently lost, and Yandex plans to enable backups by default and strengthen its infrastructure.

item.title: Platform Engineering Must Adapt to AI Agents and Nontechnical Users
item.description: The rise of AI agents and nontechnical creators is pushing platform engineering to manage a mix of human improvisation and precise automation. Platforms must incorporate machine-readable guardrails, limited identities, and Kubernetes-inspired control loops.

item.title: Cisco Will Integrate All Future Products with Its Cloud Control Platform
item.description: Cisco announced that all new products starting in 2027 will integrate with Cloud Control, a unified interface for networking, security, and observability. The service will expand internationally starting in February, while Cisco also plans to simplify ThousandEyes licensing and expand Live Protect.

item.title: IBM and Microsoft Launch Imagine Enterprise to Govern AI Agents
item.description: IBM Consulting and Microsoft launched Imagine Enterprise, an agentic AI platform aimed in part at regulated industries. It combines more than 6,000 preconfigured IBM agents with Microsoft’s Azure, Entra, Purview, Defender, and Sentinel services.

item.title: U.S. Data Center Electricity Demand Is Growing Ten Times Faster Than the Grid
item.description: U.S. data center electricity demand has increased by about 19% annually since 2000, compared with 2% for grid capacity. According to Howden, data centers may need to obtain up to 58% of their electricity off-grid by 2030.

item.title: GraphRAG Improves Knowledge Retrieval for AI Applications
item.description: GraphRAG stores knowledge as interconnected entities and relationships, improving performance over traditional RAG for multistep reasoning and broad summaries. However, this approach incurs significantly higher indexing and processing costs.

item.title: SAP Makes ABAP a Runtime Foundation for Enterprise Agentic AI
item.description: SAP is positioning the ABAP platform as an enterprise runtime foundation for agentic AI as part of its vision for the autonomous enterprise. Upcoming developments include governance, reliability, scaling, and an ABAP Model Context Protocol server.

item.title: Microsoft Reveals a Technique for Hiding a Backdoor in an AI Agent
item.description: Microsoft researchers discovered “Lazarus,” a technique capable of reprogramming dormant neurons in an AI model. An apparently normal agent can then execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

item.title: Thundermail, Thunderbird’s Email Service, Opens Early Access
item.description: Thunderbird has begun offering early access to Thundermail, its paid email-hosting service. It offers custom domains, 30 GB of storage, and integration with Thunderbird’s desktop and mobile apps.

item.title: Ottawa, Kansas, Approves a Ten-Year Moratorium on Data Centers
item.description: Voters in Ottawa approved a ten-year restriction on data centers by nearly 72%.

item.title: ByteDance is preparing a personal AI agent to compete with Meta
item.description: ByteDance is reportedly preparing a personal AI assistant capable of performing tasks such as shopping or managing a schedule. Its name, features, and launch date are not yet known.

item.title: AI Agents Spot a Maya Pyramid in Lidar Images
item.description: Forty-eight AI agents analyzed NASA lidar images covering 1,200 square kilometers of Mexican jungle and identified a site containing a pyramid. However, the site had already been mapped in 2025, contrary to the experiment’s initial claim.

item.title: A Robot Duck Learns to Follow a Cat in a Few Hours
item.description: A Wired journalist used GPT-6 Sol to program and train a virtual version of the Microduck robot to spot and follow their cat. The experiment took a few hours instead of several weeks.

item.title: Adobe Shows Prototypes for 3D Photos and AI Characters
item.description: Adobe presented prototypes that can turn an image into a 3D scene, shape an AI character’s personality through conversation, and simplify photo editing. These tools are not yet commercial products.

item.title: The Authors of “AI 2027” Predict Superhuman AI as Early as 2027
item.description: A METR report estimates that Anthropic is progressing about twice as fast as before, largely thanks to AI. The AI Futures Project now considers it likely that AI surpassing the best human researchers will arrive in 2027.

item.title: TrustedRouter Combines Multiple AI Models, Including a U.S. Version
item.description: TrustedRouter is launching Prometheus 4.0, Liberty 4.0, and Polyphemus 1.0, which combine multiple models or select the best one for each request. Requests can remain encrypted through to the processing server.

item.title: Helsing unveils AI to prepare targets for weapons systems
item.description: Helsing’s Clarity platform turns sensor data into target recommendations. The company says every decision will be attributed to a responsible human and placed under European oversight.

item.title: Researchers warn that AI progress is accelerating
item.description: Two recent reports reportedly indicate that AI is advancing faster than expected, raising concerns especially among Anthropic’s safety researchers. The Information also publishes its annual selection of 50 promising startups.

item.title: 3,500 laser robots eliminate parasites from Norwegian salmon
item.description: In Norwegian fish farms, around 3,500 underwater robots use AI vision to spot sea lice and then eliminate them with lasers. They replace the chemical baths used previously.

item.title: DeepL Voice translates tone, emotion and sarcasm in real time
item.description: DeepL Voice’s Aure model reproduces the speaker’s tone, emotion, emphasis and speaking rate in the target language. It works in eight languages, including French, during meetings, face-to-face conversations and via the API.

item.title: 35,000 applications created with Grok exposed sensitive data
item.description: Claroc discovered more than 35,000 applications generated with Grok that were accessible without logging in. Some contained patient data, plaintext passwords and internal information from SpaceXSI.

item.title: Anthropic ports Claude to AMD chips in three days
item.description: Anthropic says its internal Mythos model enabled it to port Claude to AMD chips in three days, whereas such a migration usually took several months. Claude now runs on four chip families.

item.title: Google Labs launches Tabletop, AI-generated mini-tools for groups
item.description: Tabletop lets users turn links, files, and ideas into collaborative tools such as an itinerary, a poll, or a tournament bracket. The service is limited to the United States and available by waitlist.

item.title: ElevenLabs announces 13 products at once
item.description: According to the AI Secret newsletter, ElevenLabs reportedly presented 13 new products in a single announcement. Details are not yet publicly available.

item.title: Teenager’s parents sue Google after exchanges with Gemini
item.description: According to a lawsuit, a teenager from North Carolina exchanged messages for nearly three months with Google Search’s AI Mode, powered by Gemini, about suicide. Senator Ed Markey is asking Google to allow schools to disable these features.

item.title: DeepSeek’s AI agent reportedly reaches 1.54 million daily users
item.description: This figure comes from the AI Secret newsletter, without an accessible primary source, and has not been confirmed by DeepSeek. If verified, it would show the rapid growth of Chinese AI agents among the general public.

item.title: US brokers reportedly sell training data to China
item.description: A ChinaTalk investigation claims that at least nine US companies sell training data to Chinese laboratories. The data notably includes reinforcement-learning environments, which are largely outside export controls.

item.title: Megaspeed suspected of delivering Nvidia chips to China
item.description: This Singapore-based data-center operator is suspected of moving billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips banned from export into China. Information about $7.5 billion in shipments has not been verified by CNBC.

item.title: Omnii Defense presents offline AI to detect biological weapons
item.description: Startup Radical Numerics presented a tool that runs without internet access on a laptop connected to a USB DNA sequencer. It assigns each sequence a threat score between 0 and 1, but faces criticism related to the departure of its adviser George Church.

item.title: Databricks launches an AI agent that analyzes business problems
item.description: The new version of Genie independently chains together long-running tasks using a company’s internal data. Its CEO uses it in particular to analyze internal surveys, lost sales and prepare for interviews.

item.title: Europe wants to ban dark patterns and loot boxes for minors
item.description: The proposed Digital Fairness Act targets difficult-to-cancel subscriptions, addictive design, ads targeting minors, and personalized pricing, among other practices. Fines could reach 6% of global turnover.

item.title: UK mandates university exams resistant to AI
item.description: The English regulator believes it is nearly impossible to fairly assess work completed at home. Universities will have to return to supervised examinations or face sanctions.

item.title: A $749 kit turns seawater into drinking water
item.description: Vital Lyfe designed a portable desalination unit weighing around 11 kg. It produces 22.7 liters per hour from seawater and can be installed on a boat without drilling through the hull.

item.title: Uber launches a parking-space reservation service
item.description: Uber Parking lets users compare and reserve a space through the SpotHero network, which includes 13,000 parking facilities in 400 cities across the United States and Canada. The service is not yet planned for Europe and currently has no AI component.

item.title: Meta replaces its longtime infrastructure chief
item.description: Santosh Janardhan is stepping down as Meta’s head of infrastructure, where he had worked since 2009, but will remain an adviser during the transition. Dave Brown, formerly Amazon’s head of cloud and AI, will succeed him.

item.title: CoreWeave says demand for AI computing far exceeds supply
item.description: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected results and raised its forecast, sending its stock higher. Its CEO says Nvidia H100 chips bought four years ago are still being re-rented at 20% to 50% above their purchase price.
